question: Your support agent calls the MCP tool lookup_order, whose description reads only "Looks up an order." Logs show that many calls fail because the agent passes a customer's email address, or an order number copied with a leading "#" and spaces, while the backend accepts only IDs like ORD-48213. When a customer gives only an email, the agent still calls lookup_order instead of calling get_customer first. Which change most directly reduces these failed calls?

options.text: Rename lookup_order to lookup_order_by_id and leave its one-line description unchanged, so that the new tool name alone signals which input the tool expects.
options.reason: The guide names descriptions as the primary selection mechanism; a new name without the input format, an example or the email-only edge case leaves the minimal description unreliable.

options.text: Add a system prompt rule that tells the agent to call lookup_order whenever a customer message contains the word "order," so that order requests always reach that tool.
options.reason: The guide warns that keyword-sensitive system prompt instructions create unintended tool associations, and this rule would send even email-only requests to lookup_order without fixing the input format.

options.text: Expand the lookup_order description to state the ORD-plus-digits input format with an example, and to say that an email-only request needs get_customer first.
options.reason: The guide says tool descriptions should include input formats, examples, edge cases and boundaries; this adds the expected format, an example and the email-only boundary.

options.text: Set tool_choice to force get_customer on every turn, so that the agent always identifies the customer before it is able to make any order lookup at all.
options.reason: Forced tool selection makes the model call that one tool, which blocks normal use of other tools and still gives the agent no description of the order ID format.
